Status

Current state: Under Discussion

Discussion thread: https://lists.apache.org/thread/0frtc6h3y9ts89do3qb9yk6oj3o1ktg2

JIRA: KAFKA-18800

Target release: 4.5

Please keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki (wiki discussions get unwieldy fast).

Motivation

Authorizer#aclCount() was added by KIP-801 (PR #11649, Kafka 3.2) so that the broker could publish an AclCount metric by reading the value from the authorizer. The broker side of that plan was never implemented.

KIP-877 later introduced Monitorable / PluginMetrics, which lets every plugin register its own metrics. Authorizers gained that support in 4.1 (KAFKA-18888, PR #19050), and StandardAuthorizer now publishes acls-total-count through PluginMetrics, backed by exactly the same data as Authorizer#aclCount().

With PluginMetrics available, Authorizer#aclCount() no longer has a purpose, so this KIP deprecates it. Third-party authorizers that want an ACL-count metric, or any other metric, should implement Monitorable per KIP-877.

Public Interfaces

Authorizer#aclCount() is marked @Deprecated(forRemoval = true).

java

No other public API changes. The acls-total-count metric name, type, and tag set produced by StandardAuthorizer are unchanged.

Proposed Changes

  1. Deprecate Authorizer#aclCount() in 4.5 and remove it in 5.0.
  2. Make the acls-total-count gauge in StandardAuthorizer read the count from StandardAuthorizerData directly instead of calling aclCount(). The metric value does not change.
  3. Remove StandardAuthorizer#aclCount() in 4.5.

Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan

Authorizer#aclCount() stays on the interface with the same signature and the same -1 default, so existing authorizers keep compiling and running. The only visible effect is a deprecation warning.

No metric changes for anyone. StandardAuthorizer keeps publishing acls-total-count under the same name and tags, and since the broker never used Authorizer#aclCount(), third-party authorizers never had a metric derived from it.

A third-party authorizer can define its own metrics through Monitorable (supported for authorizers since 4.1). It does not need to follow the metric names used by StandardAuthorizer. For example:

javajava()), (Gauge) (config, now) -> count.get()); } // ... existing Authorizer methods ... } ]]>

The deprecation will be listed in the 4.5 upgrade notes, and the method will be removed in Kafka 5.0.

Test Plan

PR #23521 (merged) added a unit test for the acls-total-count metric. It does not depend on this KIP.

Rejected Alternatives

  • Keep Authorizer#aclCount() as is. The broker never reads it, so keeping it could mislead third-party implementations.
  • Implement the broker-side AclCount metric planned in KIP-801. PluginMetrics (KIP-877) already lets authorizers register their own metrics.
